questions.prompt: At a 9-handed $2/$5 game with 100 big blinds, which open is the tightest?
questions.explanation: Earlier position acts first after the flop and faces more players, so the open is tighter.

questions.prompt: Which hand is a standard open from under the gun at that table?
questions.explanation: AKo is a clear early-position open. Weak offsuit broadways and low suited connectors are folds from UTG.

questions.prompt: Why is AJo usually a fold from a tight 9-handed under the gun?

choices.text: Aces are never playable in early position.
It is dominated when a later player continues with a stronger ace or king.
Offsuit hands cannot win at showdown.
The big blind is forced to call any early open.

questions.explanation: AJo looks strong and still loses often to AK, AQ, and AJ that continue behind.

questions.prompt: A normal live open with no limpers is closest to which size?

choices.text: The minimum raise, about 2 big blinds, every time.
All-in, because live cash has no postflop play.
About 3–5 big blinds, larger than a typical online open.

questions.explanation: Live opens are bigger than online 2–2.5bb opens so the field does not get a cheap flop.
